In floras 'delicate' means thin, slender, fine, tender or easily damaged, depending on the part. PATO fragile is a disposition to break and covers only one of these readings. No single existing class fits, so the word should stay unmapped.

Heteromorphic means occurring in different forms, not necessarily two. The accepted rule R0102 maps 'polymorphic' to PATO variant shape, with FLOPO dimorphic as the narrower two-form case. Mapping to dimorphic would claim exactly two forms where the text does not say so.

Reclining is ambiguous in floras: leaning on a support (semi-scandent), lying down, or bent backwards. It is not reliably decumbent (lying on the ground with rising tips). PATO:0001965 reclinate is a curled quality and does not fit either.

'Polymorphic' is mostly said of species or populations (a taxonomic remark), or of variation in colour, hairiness or size, not only shape. Mapping it to PATO variant shape on the bearer would make false phenotypes. The dimorphic and heterophylly cases need their own terms.

'Radial' is ambiguous: radial symmetry of flowers, radial walls and sections, radially arranged ribs or rays. Radiating fits only the last. The flower sense already has R0607 (radially symmetric to actinomorphic); a flower-only rule for 'radial' to PATO:0001328 actinomorphic can be added separately.

Well-defined usually means sharply delimited or distinct from the neighbouring part (well-defined petiole, keel, border), not clearly visible. There is no PATO or FLOPO term for 'distinct', and PATO:0005006 differentiated from needs the second part.
Gland-like means resembling a gland (gland-like teeth, appendages), not bearing glands or being glandular tissue. Mapping it to PATO:0002117 glandular would claim glands are present.

Veiny means conspicuously veined, which is a visibility statement, not presence. The target PO:0005020 is the vascular bundle, not leaf lamina vein (PO:0020138). The right form is vein + conspicuous (a pattern with a part), not a single-word rule.
'Level' is vague (flat, even, 'at the level of', 'level with' X). PATO flush needs a second surface, which the word alone does not give.
Laminate means either having a blade or layered (bark, testa). It does not reliably mean that a lamina is present.
Poorly defined margins, zones or veins are indistinctly delimited, which is not the same as low visibility. There is no 'indistinct' term. This matches the drop of 'well-defined' (R0160).
Stigmatic means 'of the stigma' (stigmatic surface, lobes, branches). It names part of the stigma, so it belongs with the bearer, and it does not state that a stigma is present.

Heterophylly means leaves of different forms on one plant, and there can be more than two. FLOPO dimorphic (FLOPO:0991092) states exactly two forms, which adds a claim the text does not make. No existing parent class means 'of several forms', so this needs a new class (a parent of dimorphic and sibl

In 'stipe-like base' or 'stipe-like internode', the bearer is the stalk-like part itself. Stipitate (FLOPO:0991065, borne on a stalk) would wrongly say that part is carried on a stalk. FLOPO deals with resemblance words through 'X-like' shape classes (petiole-like FLOPO:0991298, stolon-like). Stipe-

'Underdeveloped' can mean reduced or rudimentary, or simply not yet developed (young). 'Decreased size' loses that meaning. PATO vestigial (a remnant structure) and hypoplastic (fewer cells) do not fit either. Too ambiguous for one class.
On a stem, 'denuded' can mean stripped of leaves, hairs, scales or bark. Leaf absent is only one of these, and the rule would also wrongly say an older stem section never had leaves.
'Irregularly' contradicts the exact right-angled outline of PATO rectangular, so the mapping would state a precise shape the text denies.

'Withering' describes a process, often of persistent parts ('withering and persistent'). PATO shriveled is a resulting state, and marcescent (FLOPO:0991181) also needs persistence. The word is not a reliable cue for either.
'Contracted' (shortened or crowded overall, as in a panicle) is not 'constricted' (narrowed at one point). The negation maps to the wrong quality.
FLOPO:0991012 leafy means bearing well-developed foliage. 'Sparsely leafy' says nearly the opposite, so the mapping would mislead.

FLOPO:0991045 floating means resting on the water surface, and its own note asks to keep free-floating plants apart. 'Free-floating' (not attached to the ground, possibly submerged) needs its own class or a pattern.

Apiculate (a short, sharp, flexible point) is not mucronulate (FLOPO:0991055, a minute mucro, under mucronate). FLOPO has no apiculate value class, and PATO has 'apiculate' only as a synonym of the sharpness attribute.

The softness belongs to the wood (PO secondary xylem, which has 'wood' as a synonym), not to the bearer named in the text. A word rule cannot move the quality to a different part, so this needs a pattern.
On its own, 'unpleasant' can describe taste as well as smell. FLOPO:0991020 foetid already has 'unpleasant smell' as a synonym, which covers the clear case.
The quality 'inconspicuous' belongs to the veins (PO vascular bundle / vein), not to the leaf. This needs the pattern that puts the quality on the part's veins, not a word rule.
'Nervose' means conspicuously veined. 'Vascular bundle present' is true of almost every leaf, so it loses the whole meaning. FLOPO has no prominently-veined class.
'Expanding' is ambiguous: it can describe growth over time ('expanding leaves') or widening along a part ('expanding into a sheath'). It does not reliably mean PATO dilated.
'Bristle' is a synonym of both PO trichome and PO awn, and in Asteraceae it means pappus bristles. 'Bristleless' does not mean all trichomes are absent.
'Not produced' is a general phrase ('not produced beyond the apex'). It has no fixed link to FLOPO:0991162 excurrent.
The striation belongs to the venation, not the bearer. Putting PATO striated on the bearer is wrong without the vein pattern.
'Semi-exserted' means only partly projecting. PATO exserted would say the part fully projects, which the text does not say.

Glandular-pubescent (FLOPO_0991173) requires short soft hairs, but pilose means long hairs, so the rule is wrong. No glandular-pilose class exists. Pilose (FLOPO_0991048) alone would lose the glands, and glandular (PATO_0002117) alone would lose the hair type. It needs a new class or two separate an

'Fully developed' is mostly a stage word ('fully developed leaves/fruits'), which belongs to the stage pattern, not to a quality. Only occasionally does it contrast with a reduced staminode. 'Not vestigial' is not what the text says.

Setulose means bearing small stiff bristles, but glandular-pubescent (FLOPO_0991173) means soft hairs, so the rule is wrong. No glandular-setulose class exists. Setose (PATO_0002289) would lose the glands and glandular (PATO_0002117) would lose the bristles.

'Bulged' means swollen or protruding, but not necessarily on one side. Gibbous (FLOPO_0991130) requires one-sided swelling, so it is too narrow. PATO swollen is already used for flora 'swollen' bases and nodes, as the accepted pairs in flora_union_pairs.tsv show.

Connivent (FLOPO_0991147) requires the parts to converge and touch. 'Converging' only says they lean toward each other, as stamens or follicles do. Neither PATO nor FLOPO has a convergent class, so no existing class fits.

A biparous cyme is a dichasium, and PO lists dichasium as a synonym of cyme inflorescence. The rule should become an entity-presence rule ('cyme inflorescence present'), the same as R0023 dichasial. Bifurcated (PATO_0001784) is wrong.
Hypocrepiform means horseshoe-shaped. It is not hypocrateriform, which is salverform (FLOPO_0991144). No horseshoe-shape class exists in PATO or FLOPO. It needs a new class or should be rejected.

In the floras 'columellate' describes pollen exine (rod-like columellae) and lichen apothecia. PO_0025230 columella covers fruit and moss-capsule columellae, which are different structures, and no PO class fits the other senses.

A plain pato rule puts the quality on the part named in the sentence, so 'leaves obscurely nerved' would give 'leaf inconspicuous', which is false. The rule kind cannot set the veins (PO:0005020) as the part. 'Obscure' (C174) already covers 'obscure veins', where the veins are named.
Flask-shaped (FLOPO:0991183) needs a body swollen below plus a neck. 'Narrow-necked' states only the neck, and the rule's own note found a case that does not fit. Too doubtful for 4 statements.

In 'leaf base narrowed and petiolelike', the taper comes from 'narrowed'. 'Petiolelike' alone means stalk-like (e.g. a pseudopetiole or claw), not 'tapering to a slender point' as PATO:0001982 attenuate is defined.
Fragile fits only 'readily tearing'. The bare word also describes how spathes or sheaths split or open (dehiscence), so the rule is ambiguous.
Delimited means marked off or bounded, often by different cells (e.g. moss alar cells). It is not visibility of the part. The bare key would also fire inside 'poorly delimited'.

'Sheathed' usually means enclosed by a sheath (passive), while FLOPO:0991105 sheathing means the part itself wraps the axis. 'Not sheathed' (e.g. spines 'neither sheathed nor barbed') does not clearly negate sheathing.

The word is said of the plant, and a pato rule cannot move the quality to the stem. The result would be 'whole plant decreased strength', which is wrong. It needs a rule kind or pattern that sets stem (PO_0009047) as the part.
'Graceful' describes how a part looks. PATO slender lists 'gracile' only as a related synonym, and for whole plants the word is vague. Too doubtful for a rule.

'Increasing' on its own is a general word: increasing in size, number or diameter, or a change along the part. Accrescent applies only when the text names it or says the part enlarges after flowering, and those cases have their own rules.

Tooth-shaped (dentiform) is about how a part looks, not a fixed outline. Teeth can be narrow, hooked or rounded, so triangular claims too much. There is no dentiform class in PATO or FLOPO, and with only 7 statements a new term is not worth adding.

In 'hairs glandular-tipped' the bearer is the hair, which has a gland at its tip. Handle it like the reviewed 'gland-tipped' rule (R0010): gland present at the apex. Glandular-pubescent describes a surface clothed with such hairs and is wrong on the hair itself. Stipitate-glandular has the same prob
The key leaves out where the vein ends. 'Midvein extending' can continue 'to the apex' (percurrent), 'beyond the apex' (excurrent, FLOPO_0991162) or 'to the middle'. Map the full phrases instead.

Glossaries define obcuneate/obcuneiform as wedge-shaped with the narrow end at the apex, the reverse of cuneate. Floras use it loosely, so the word is ambiguous. With 5 statements, reject rather than force cuneate.

FLOPO unequal is defined for like parts within one set that differ in size. 'Variable-sized' in a taxon description often means variation between plants or specimens, which is a different character. The word is ambiguous between the two readings.

The wrinkling is in the veins or network, not on the whole surface, so plain rugose puts it on the wrong part. No existing class says 'rugose venation' as a single value. It needs the part-of-bearer pattern rather than a word rule.
'X surrounded by hairs' describes hairs on another structure placed around X. That is a relation between two parts (pattern 09), and saying 'trichome present' of X puts the hairs on the wrong bearer.

Perennating describes organs (buds, rhizomes, bulbs, corms) that carry the plant through the bad season. The organ itself need not live more than two years, so 'perennial life span' does not fit those bearers. No existing class covers this survival role.

The word is ambiguous. It can mean two or more parts of the same width (an equal-size reading, which FLOPO_0991102 covers only for overall size), the same width throughout (parallel-sided), or 'as wide as long'. No single class fits all three.

Discolorous (FLOPO:0991070) is a quality of the whole leaf, whose two surfaces differ. 'Lighter coloured' is usually said of one surface (the bearer would then be the under surface) or compares one taxon with another. With only 3 statements, the general phrase is too unsafe to map to discolorous.

Hydrophobic (PATO:0001885) is a chemical tendency of a surface to repel water. Floras use 'water-shedding' for leaves that drain water by their shape or overlap as well as by their surface. The rule's own reason admits the shape reading. With 3 statements and two meanings, no rule should be made.

In moss descriptions 'without clearly defined stereids' means the thick-walled cells are not set apart as a band. They may still be present, and the clear absence is already covered by R1908 'without stereids'. Mapping it to 'stereid absent' claims more than the text says.

Calcified (PATO:0001447) claims a calcium carbonate crust. In floras, 'incrusted' also means a crust of silica, resin or salt, or (in French, 'incrustée') a sunken midrib. The word alone does not support calcified. A phrase rule such as 'incrusted with lime' would be safe.
'Indistinctly delimited' means the boundaries are unclear. PATO inconspicuous (PATO_0000464) is about visibility, not about distinct edges. No existing class means 'without a clear boundary'.
'Bunch' is a noun (a bunch of fruit or flowers). It does not say that stems grow in a dense tuft from the base, which is what caespitose (FLOPO_0991007) means.
Hummock grasses (e.g. Triodia) form mounds and are told apart from tussock grasses. Neither caespitose (FLOPO_0991007) nor mat-forming (FLOPO_0991010) fits, and no mound or cushion class exists.
'Tolerant to' (PATO_0000515) needs the thing tolerated. Without 'drought' the statement says nothing. It needs a pattern that records the stimulus, not a word rule.
'Coniferous' describes a taxon or a type of forest, not a part that has a strobilus. Strobilus present (PO_0025083) does not fit any bearer.
Not fragrant does not mean odourless (PATO_0001208). The part may smell bad or have some other smell. There is no fragrant class to negate (fragrant is only a related synonym of sweet-scented).
Pseudo-fascicled means the parts only look clustered and are not truly fascicled (FLOPO_0991098). No 'pseudofasciculate' class exists, unlike pseudoverticillate.
'Venulose' describes conspicuous, dense fine veinlets. Every leaf has vascular bundles (PO_0005020) and veinlets, so a presence statement adds nothing and misses the point.
Broadest at the middle covers elliptic, oblong, orbicular and linear shapes. It says where the widest point is, not which shape the part has.
The prominence belongs to the veins, not to the part described. It needs a vein + prominent pattern (vascular bundle PO_0005020 with prominent PATO_0001482), not a word rule on the part.
The word is ambiguous: 'glandular and hairless' or 'without glandular hairs'. Rejecting it is better than a guess.
'Irregularly cut' also covers incised, laciniate and erose margins, not just torn-looking ones (lacerate, FLOPO_0991115). PATO cut (PATO_0001978) requires regular cuts, so it does not fit either.
Bicucullate means the part carries two hoods. The part itself is not hood-shaped, so cucullate (FLOPO_0991119) on it is wrong, and no existing class means 'two-hooded'.

Petioluliform says a leaflet or blade base narrows into a stalk like a petiolule. FLOPO clawed (unguiculate) is the petal term for an abrupt claw. The earlier rules for the same idea used other terms: petiolelike went to attenuate (R0804) and falsely petiolate to tapered (R0912). With only 5 stateme

'Without basal glands' says the glands are missing only at the base. The rule would say the gland is absent from the whole bearer, which can be false. Absence in one region needs the region-of-the-bearer pattern, not a quality rule.

The quality belongs to the leaf sinus (PO_0025384), but the rule sets only the quality. Decreased width would land on the leaf or lobe, which are not narrow. This needs the sinus to be put in as the bearer (part-of-bearer pattern), not a quality rule.

'Composite' is ambiguous. In French floras 'composées' (leaves) means compound, and in English it can mean compound or Asteraceae-like. As a quality word it would put a capitulum on leaves and other parts.

The thin part is the fruit valve (PO_0000033), but the rule would put decreased thickness on the whole fruit, which would mean a flattened fruit. The valve has to be put in as the bearer (part-of-bearer pattern); a quality rule cannot do that.

PATO elliptic has ellipsoid as an exact synonym, and 'broadly' and 'narrowly ellipsoid' (R0039, R0295, R1367) were all mapped to it. A short ellipsoid is barely longer than wide, so prolate (polar axis longer) adds an elongation the word plays down. R1316 broad-ellipsoid → prolate is the outlier.

Bryologists use 'lax' for cells that are large and thin-walled, but the thinness belongs to the cell wall, not the cell, and 'lax' does not state a thickness. This needs the part-of-the-bearer pattern (cell wall decreased thickness), not a word rule.
The strength belongs to the stem. A word rule leaves robust on the whole plant. The right annotation is stem (PO:0009047) robust, which needs the part-of-the-bearer pattern.
The thickness belongs to the lateral walls of cells, not to the part named. Increased thickness on the bearer would be wrong. This needs the cell-wall part pattern.
A positive class now exists for a set of homologous structures occurring in a single form. That is exactly homomorphous, and better than a negation of dimorphic.

'Stems remotely branched' puts distance between the branches, not on the stem. A quality rule cannot move the bearer to the branches (only part-name rules move it), so this rule would label the stem 'distant', which is wrong.

The size belongs to the lumen, not to the cell or leaf that the statement describes. Quality rules cannot move the bearer (only part-name rules move it), so this would wrongly make the cell 'increased size'. It needs a lumen bearer rule instead.
Microphyllous branches have small leaves. The size belongs to the leaves, but the rule would put 'decreased size' on the branch or plant. A quality rule cannot move the bearer.
'Without margin' does not reliably mean 'not winged'. There is no usable 'margin' part class (it was rejected as a generic part), and 'not winged' is a guess, so it is better left unannotated.
'Slightly developed' is about degree of development, not size. 'Decreased size' is unsupported and 'vestigial' (PATO_0000588) is too strong. The phrase is ambiguous.
Embedded (enclosed in a tissue or pulp) and sunken (below the level of the surrounding surface) differ. Negating one does not negate the other.
FLOPO_0991035 subterranean means below the ground surface. Semi-subterranean means only partly so, and no existing class means 'partly buried'.
A lambda shape is an inverted, unequal-legged figure, neither a symmetric V (PATO_0002224) nor a Y (PATO_0001201). Rare and ambiguous.
'Keel' is a noun for a part (PO_0025327 keel, PO_0025326 keel petal), not a quality. As a quality word it would mislabel the bearer. The shape belongs to 'keeled' or 'carinate'.
Enrolled means rolled, not curled (PATO_0000405). Floras use it both for margins rolled under (revolute, PATO_0001963) and rolled upward (involute, PATO_0001962), so no single target is safe.
Sacking-like is a simile for a coarse, woven-looking texture (bark, leaf-sheath fibres). FLOPO_0991026 fibrous is not equivalent.
Balsamic describes a balsam smell. FLOPO_0991075 resinous is a resin coating on the surface. Different quality. PATO aromatic (PATO_0002191) is a chemical quality, not a smell.

The whole phrase hides 'basally', which flora_context_words.tsv already maps to the base region. 'Dilated' would then apply to the whole part. Leave it to the separate 'basally' rule plus an 'expanded' rule.
Same as R1742: the phrase rule bypasses the 'basally' base-region rule and labels the whole part inflated.
Craspedodromous (PATO_0001969) is about secondary veins ending at the margin. 'Ending in teeth' is said of lobes, calyx tubes and awns too, so the phrase does not mean this venation.
Granular-glandular (glandular granules on the surface) is not clearly the same as FLOPO_0991174 gland-dotted (dots that are glands on or in the tissue).
PO lists pseudobulb as a synonym of corm (PO_0025355), but orchid pseudobulbs are swollen aerial stem internodes, not underground corms. Mapping would be wrong for most flora uses.
PO lists rootstock as a synonym of rhizome (PO_0004542), but floras use 'root-stock' for a caudex, a woody base or a tuberous root too. Too ambiguous for 'rhizome present'.
A scape is a leafless peduncle arising from the ground. Scapeless plants can still have peduncles, so 'peduncle absent' (PO_0009053) is wrong, and PO has no scape class.
Setulose means minutely bristly and ciliolate means minutely fringed. Setose (PATO_0002289) overstates the bristles and loses the fringe. The compound needs two mappings or none.
'Without median groove' allows other grooves. 'Not grooved' (PATO_0002255) would claim no grooves at all.
'Wooded' in floras describes habitat (wooded slopes). The plant-part word is 'woody'. Mapping to ligneous would mislabel habitat text.
Aperturate means a pollen grain has germination apertures, not perforate (pierced with holes, PATO_0002112). PO has no pollen aperture class to use instead.
'Broader than wide' is self-contradictory, probably a slip for 'broader than long'. A length-to-width comparison is not plain broad (PATO_0002359).
PATO conspicuous is 'clearly visible'. Discernible means only 'can just be seen' and often appears in phrases like 'scarcely discernible', so mapping it to conspicuous would invert the meaning.
Distinctive means characteristic of a taxon, not a visibility quality. There is no fitting class.
'Finely veined' is about how fine or dense the venation is, not whether veins are present. Vascular bundle present says almost nothing, and no fineness or vein-density class exists.
An irregular outline contradicts a regular elliptic shape. PATO irregularly shaped would lose the oval shape. No single class fits.
Ovoid is a 3-D egg shape and PATO ovate is 2-D, and 'narrow' is lost. No ovoid class exists in FLOPO (only obovoid FLOPO:0991025). Leave unmapped until the pato#627 ovoid class arrives.
'Nearly solid' means a small cavity or pith is present. 'Not hollow' states the part is fully solid, which overstates it.
This is about how far the part is developed (reduced or weakly formed), not visibility. Hypoplastic would also be a stretch. Ambiguous; no rule.
'Pealike' means resembling a pea flower (papilionaceous) or a pea in shape, not the size class pea-sized. Ambiguous.
PO lamina (synonym blade) is the general blade of leaves, petals, sepals and tepals. Using it for 'with blade' presence avoids limiting leaf lamina to leaves only.
Cilia are marginal hairs. Trichome absent says the part has no hairs at all, which is false when the surface is still hairy. No cilium class exists in PO.
'Without distinct blade' means the blade is indistinct or merges with the petiole, not that the lamina is absent.
'Alike' means 'not dimorphic' only when comparing morphs. A bearer-part constraint cannot capture that context, and elsewhere it just means similar.
FLOPO equal is defined as a size quality of a set of like parts. 'Equally developed' is about the degree of development, so mapping it to equal is doubtful.
Compound (divided into separate leaflets) is not lobed. The correct idea is the PO entity compound leaf, which a quality rule cannot express safely for every bearer.
Crust is a lichen or algal growth form (or a surface crust), not FLOPO mat-forming. Ambiguous.
Lacking chlorophyll is not the same as colourless; such plants are often coloured. No chlorophyll-absent class was found to use instead.
Thin-walled describes the wall, not the bearer. Decreased thickness on the bearer would be wrong, and a rule cannot switch the bearer to the cell wall.
A mitten shape has one lateral lobe, like a thumb, so it is not bilobed. It needs a new class or should stay unmapped.
'Moderately tall' is a mid-range height. PATO increased height means taller than a reference, which overstates it.

'Perigonial' is an adjective that needs its noun (perigonial leaves, bracts or buds). On its own it does not say that a perigonial bract (PO_0030028) is present. The part should come from the noun as the bearer.

A protonemal rhizoid (PO_0030079) is wrong. 'Protonematous' usually describes gemmae, flagella or rhizoids that are protonema-like, or a persistent protonema. Retargeting to protonema (PO_0030003) present would be either always true for mosses or the wrong meaning. It is ambiguous, so no rule.

This is a part plus a quality: the leaf bases have broken up into fibres. Saying only that a leaf base (PO_0020040) is present loses the point. It needs leaf base as the bearer with a fibrous or shredded quality, not a word rule.
'Traces of fibrils' means that only a few fibrils remain. Fibrillary (PATO_0002134) says the structure is fibrous. No existing class means 'faintly or vestigially fibrillose'.
'Tolerant to' (PATO_0000515) is a relation and needs the thing tolerated. Without salt the statement is empty. This needs a pattern with salt as the object, or a halophyte or salt-tolerant class.

These are two separate qualities: the covering is white (colour) and mealy (PATO_0104364, texture). One rule to mealy throws the colour statement away. The word should be split into white + mealy, not mapped to one class.
'Battened' is not a botanical word for buttressed (FLOPO_0991138), and no source links them. It is probably a bad translation. The meaning is unclear.

Brachystylous names the short-styled morph of a flower, not the heterostylous condition of the species (FLOPO_0991137). Descriptions often contrast brachystylous and dolichostylous flowers, so both words would collapse into one class. It needs a morph class, for example a child of distylous (FLOPO_0
Brown and mottled are two separate qualities: colour, and a pattern (PATO_0002274). One rule loses the colour. The word should be split into brown + mottled.

This is a quality plus a place. 'At base' is already a region context word (config/flora_context_words.tsv), so the base becomes the bearer. A whole-phrase rule to tapered would bypass that step and put the quality on the whole organ.
This is connate (FLOPO_0991067) plus a place. 'At base' is a region context word, so the base becomes the bearer. A whole-phrase rule would wrongly say the parts are fused along their whole length.
Circumferential (running around the circumference, as in a circumferential slit, ring or dehiscence line) is not surrounding another structure (PATO_0001772). No existing class fits all its uses.
'Flattenuated' is not a botanical word. It may be a typo for flattened or attenuated, or a blend of the two. Since we cannot tell which, no rule.

Hickey's leaf-architecture scheme, which PATO cites for actinodromous, lists flabellate venation as its own type: many equally fine veins fanning out from the base and forking towards the tip. So actinodromous makes a false claim. Fan-shaped (PATO_0002219) is a shape of the blade, not of the veins.

Pulpy maps to fleshy (R0084), so pulpy is narrower than fleshy. Negating the narrower word does not negate the broader one: a firm fleshy fruit is 'not pulpy' but is still fleshy. 'Not fleshy' would be a false statement.

In plinerved leaves (for example Melastomataceae, Cinnamomum) the lateral primary veins leave the midrib above the base and often curve to the apex, which is acrodromous. Actinodromous claims more than the text says. FLOPO triplinerved (FLOPO_0991202) is too narrow, because there may be 5 veins. A b

'Lateral bracts' are only some of the bracts, often paired bracteoles or prophylls. A part with a median bract but no lateral ones would wrongly get 'bract absent'. Bracteole (PO_0009043) does not fit the 'beside the receptacle' sense either.
The text only denies a central bundle of paraphyses. 'Paraphysis absent' claims there are none at all, and paraphyses may still sit among the sporangia. No existing class says this correctly.

The meaning depends on the plant family. 'Floral tube' is the hypanthium in Onagraceae, Lythraceae and Thymelaeaceae, but the perianth tube (FLOPO_0986010) in Iridaceae, Amaryllidaceae and others. A part-name constraint cannot express a family, so a bare rule would mislabel one group either way.

Generic 'anther appendage' can be a connective appendage (FLOPO_0986073) or a theca appendage such as the awns and spurs in Ericaceae (FLOPO_0986131); both classes exist. Mapping to the connective is wrong for the theca kind. Mapping to the anther would wrongly give the anther the appendage's size o
Plural of R2255; same ambiguity between connective appendage and theca appendage.
French generic form of R2255; ambiguous between connective appendage and theca appendage.

'Bloom' as a part name is ambiguous (flowers or flowering versus a waxy coat). The waxy sense is already covered by the quality rule 'bloom' → glaucous (R0960, as for pruinose C222), which keeps the organ as the bearer.

It is ambiguous. A 'sterile sheath' may be a bladeless basal leaf (scale leaf), a sterile bract on an orchid or Eriocaulaceae peduncle (bract), or a sheath around a sterile part. No single existing class is safe.

Floras use 'pseudo-staminodium' for structures that look like staminodes but are set apart from true staminodes, often because they may not come from a stamen. Mapping it to staminode (PO_0009077, 'sterile stamen') states an origin the text denies. With no safe general class, it is better rejected,
'Aristés' is the French adjective 'awned', not a part name. It should become a rule saying an awn (PO_0025349) is present, on the glume or lemma it describes, not a bearer rule.

A hair-point is a slender, often hyaline extension beyond the leaf apex (PO_0020137). Its length or toothing is not a quality of the apex. Awn (PO_0025349) is defined only for glumes, lemmas and paleas, so it does not fit either. The shape is already covered by the value term hair-pointed (FLOPO:099
Plural of R2406. Same reason.
Variant spelling of R2406. Same reason.
Same as R2406. On top of that, the key contains a quality ('hyaline'), which a bearer rule would lose.

'Stock' is ambiguous: it can be a rootstock (rhizome), a caudex, which can include the root crown, or a grafting stock. The previous review handled 'caudex' and 'root-stock' as separate words. A bare 'stock' rule would carry these meanings into stem. Reject it and let the existing caudex and rootsto
'With domatia' says the part is present; it is not a part name. The quality rule R1180 (domatium present) already handles it, and this bearer rule would compete with it.

word: marge des lobes de la corolle
why: French form of R2435. It needs a rule saying the domatium (FLOPO_0986021) is present, not a bearer rule.

The exostome is only the outer ring of a double peristome. FLOPO already has a separate endostome class (FLOPO:0986064), so mapping the exostome to the whole peristome would mix outer-ring qualities (colour, papillae, striation) with the inner ring. It needs its own exostome class, the counterpart o

Outer peristome is the same as exostome. 'Inner peristome' already goes to endostome (FLOPO:0986064), so sending the outer one to the whole peristome would be lopsided and would mix in endostome qualities. It needs an exostome class.

Endostome cilia are thread-like strands between the endostome segments. Mapping them to peristome tooth would merge their counts ('cilia 2-3', 'nodose', 'rudimentary') with the 16 exostome teeth and the endostome segments, which gives false counts. Like 'appendiculae' (rejected), they need their own
Same as R2458: cilia are not teeth, and their counts would be mixed with the tooth counts.
Same as R2458.

This rule uses up the word 'basal', so the position is lost. Counts of basal glands would become counts of all glands. The plain 'gland' rule (PO_0005656) plus the region-of-the-bearer pattern already records the position, as R1438 does, so no special rule is needed.
Same as R2471.
French for basal gland. Same as R2471.
Reticulate venation is a quality: FLOPO:0991100 reticulate on the leaf venation (PO_0000036). It is not a vein, and the word should go to the quality, not to a part.

Ambiguous. In Asteraceae and Cyperaceae a 'stigmatic branch' is a style branch (FLOPO:0986008). In Euphorbiaceae and Malvaceae it is a stigma lobe (FLOPO:0986009). It is never the whole stigma, so counts would be wrong. Without the family, no single target is safe.
French for stigmatic branch. Ambiguous between style branch and stigma lobe, as in R2479.
Plural of R2480. Same ambiguity.

Reticulation is a pattern, the quality reticulate (FLOPO:0991100), on veins, seed coats, pollen or bulb coats. It is not a part. This matches the earlier rejection of 'reticulum' and 'network' as bearers.
French reticulation: a pattern, not a vein. Same as R2486.
The venation reticulum is the vein network as a whole. 'Reticulum' was already rejected as a bearer word. Where it matters, the network goes to reticulate on the leaf venation, not to a single vein.

Interprimary veins are a particular rank of vein lying between the primary veins. Mapping them to any leaf lamina vein would turn counts such as 'interprimary veins 2-4' into counts of all veins, which is wrong. PO has no class for this rank.
Plural of R2492. Same problem.

PO's note on alar cell only says the area they form is sometimes called the alar region. The region's size and shape (triangular, reaching the margin) are not the size or shape of one alar cell. This needs a region or cell-group class, not a single-cell mapping.
An alar group is a group of cells. Its size and shape would wrongly be given to single alar cells, and there is no class for the group.
An alar area is a region of the leaf base. Same problem as R2501.
Bare 'médiane' is an adjective (median lobe, tooth, sepal). 'nervure médiane' already has its own rule (R2304), so this bare word is not needed.

A pseudostyle (Schisandraceae, some Annonaceae) is a sterile extension of the carpel, not a style. Mapping it to style gives it a wrong meaning, and carpel would wrongly receive its length. It needs its own class.
Plural of R2513; same reasoning.

'Spicate' is an adjective. The quality rule spike-like (FLOPO:0991142) already covers it. As a bearer key it would turn an inflorescence described as spike-like into a true spike. The few examples where it stood for 'spikes' are better grounded by the noun itself.

In Passiflora the limen is a separate ring or cup at the base of the androgynophore. Its neighbours are the operculum and the nectary ring. It is not the series of corona filaments, which earlier rules mapped to corona lobe. Mapping it to floral corona would mix the limen's qualities with the corona

Protonemal flaps (Tetraphis and its relatives) are leaf-like plates growing on the lasting protonema. Their shape and size would be wrongly put on the whole protonema. PO has no class for the flap, and the term is used in only one small group, so it should stay unmapped.
Other spelling of R2676. Dropped for the same reason.

On its own, French 'flore' means a flora (the book), not a flower ('fleur'). The rule's own reason is about the '-flore(s)' counting suffix, which belongs in flora_counted_parts.tsv as a count, not in a bearer rule.

'-flore' means '-flowered' (3-flore, pauciflore). It is a count of flowers on the unit being described. Add it to flora_counted_parts.tsv next to 'flowered'. A bearer rule would wrongly make the flower the part that carries the quality.
Plural of R2681 ('3-7-flores'). It belongs in flora_counted_parts.tsv as a flower count, not as a bearer rule.

The word includes 'present', so as a bearer rule it loses the quality. The right form is an entity_presence rule (leaf midvein PO_0020139 + present PATO_0000467), and that is a different kind of rule, not a different target. 'midrib' alone is already a PO synonym of leaf midvein.

Corona appendages (horns, teeth, scales) are outgrowths on the corona or its lobes, not the lobes. Their shape and length would be wrongly given to corona lobe (FLOPO_0986035). Giving them to floral corona (FLOPO_0985020) would be wrong too. No existing class fits. A new appendage class would be nee
Same as R2727, in the plural.

PO defines petal spur (PO_0025511) as a slender, hollow extension. A sac is a short pouch, not slender. Moving the rule to orchid labellum (FLOPO_0980978) would give the sac's length and shape to the whole lip. No class fits. A saccate lip is better recorded as labellum + saccate (FLOPO_0991140).
Same as R2757.

'Parallel' is already handled as a quality: rule R0005 maps 'parallel' to parallelodromous (PATO_0001968) when it is about veins or nerves. 'Vein' and 'nerve' already map to vascular bundle on their own. Treating the whole phrase as one part hides the venation pattern, so the words are better ground
Same as R2767.
Same as R2767 (French).

The phrase includes the quality 'present', like the rejected 'stipe present'. A hair-point (the hyaline tip of a moss leaf) is part of the leaf apex, not the whole apex. It needs a presence statement or a hair-pointed apex value, not a bearer rule.

In seed-plant floras 'sex organs' means androecium plus gynoecium, which is a union with no single class. Gametangium (PO_0025124) fits only bryophytes and ferns, and a part constraint cannot separate the two meanings.
Same as 'sex organ': stamens plus pistil in flowering plants, gametangia only in bryophytes. No single class covers it.
In French floras 'organes sexuels' means androecium and gynoecium together. Gametangium is wrong, and no single class covers both.
'Colpé' (having colpi) is an adjective, not a part. Counts like '3-colpé' belong to the count-of-parts pattern on the colpus.

It can mean a conifer cone scale (megasporophyll PO_0009027, which already has its own 'cone scale' rule), a fruiting glume or scale in Cyperaceae, or the bracteoles of Atriplex. Fertile lemma is wrong, and the word is ambiguous.
Disk scales are separate scale-like parts of the disc, and what they are varies by family. The whole floral disc (FLOPO_0986025) is the wrong bearer, and no class for a part of the disc exists.
This is ambiguous. It can be an epidermal scale (a trichome, as in ferns) or a scale leaf (cataphyll, PO_0006003, in seed plants). No single class or part constraint resolves it.

Qualities like 'small' describe the cells, so mapping to the strand puts cell size on the strand. Hydroid (PO_0025032) does not fit 'poorly or not differentiated' cells. Use plant cell (PO_0009002) inside the central strand (a part-of pattern), not a word rule.

'2-fruited' is a count suffix like '-flowered' and '-seeded', which config/flora_counted_parts.tsv handles (flowered->flower, seeded->seed). Add 'fruited -> fruit' there (pattern 03). As a part rule, the word would turn 'fruited' (in fruit) into a fruit part.

'Punctation' is ambiguous. It can mean gland dots (Myrtaceae, Rutaceae, Hypericaceae), but also pits on seed coats or pollen, and pigment dots. The surface reading is the quality punctate / gland-dotted. A word rule to secretory tissue would mislabel the pit and dot senses.

Inflorescence bract is wrong. In Asteraceae (Ambrosia, Iva, Parthenium), 'pistillate paleae' are receptacle chaff, which is flower bract PO_0009034 (synonym chaff, as in R0121). In grasses, a palea of a pistillate floret is palea PO_0009038. The word alone does not tell which, so no single target is
Singular of R3016, same ambiguity between Asteraceae chaff (PO_0009034) and the grass palea (PO_0009038). Inflorescence bract is wrong for both.
Same as R3016. Paleae of florets are either receptacle chaff (flower bract) or grass paleae (PO_0009038), never inflorescence bracts. The phrase does not show which family is meant.

Ambiguous: it can mean a seedling's first leaf or the lowest leaf of a shoot or culm. The seedling sense is already covered by 'seedling leaf' (R3716), which maps to 'vascular leaf part of seedling' and notes that juvenile vascular leaf PO_0006339 is a stage class, not the seedling's leaf. Without t
Same ambiguity as R3027 (seedling leaf versus lowest leaf). The juvenile-stage class is not the right target for the seedling sense either.
Plural of R3028, same reasoning.

'Vaginant laminae' with 'equal/unequal' and '1/2 leaf length' is the Fissidens moss wording for the two clasping blades of the leaf. PO leaf sheath is defined as part of a vascular leaf, which a moss leaf is not. No existing class fits: this needs a FLOPO moss-leaf part class or should stay unmapped

'Involucre-like' says these are leaves arranged like an involucre, not the bracts of a true involucre. Mapping them to involucral bract states more than the flora does, and mapping them to leaf would turn their count into a leaf count for the whole plant. Leave unmapped.
Plural of R3092, same reasoning.
Hyphenated form of R3093, same reasoning.

Mapping the whole phrase to trichome loses 'simple'. Without this rule the phrase splits into bearer trichome (PO_0000282, synonym 'hair') plus quality simple (PATO_0001503) or unbranched (PATO_0000414), which is the right annotation.
Singular of R3095. Let the normal parse give trichome (PO_0000282) plus simple (PATO_0001503).

The context word 'lateral' (FLOPO_0991380) already applies to pinnules. Without this rule, 'lateral' plus 'pinnule' (FLOPO_0985028) gives pinnule plus lateral. The phrase rule would hide the position.
Same as R3103. The French 'latérale' has no context word yet. Adding 'latéral(e)(s)/latéraux' to flora_context_words.tsv (FLOPO_0991380) would be better than a phrase rule that loses the position.

Perianth lobe is its own FLOPO-local class (FLOPO_0986004), and there is no 'perianth lobe margin' class. The margin of the free lobe of a fused perianth is not strictly PO tepal margin. This needs a margin-of-part pattern or a new class, not a rule.

The context word 'lateral' (FLOPO_0991380) applies to petals. Without the rule, petal (PO_0009032) plus lateral keeps the position. Wing petal (PO_0025325) fits legumes only, not Polygala, Viola or orchids, so it cannot be the general target.
Plural of R3117.
French form of R3117. A French context word 'latéral' should carry the position, rather than a rule that loses it.
French plural of R3117. Same as R3119.

The context word 'outer' (FLOPO_0991379, added 2026-11-14) applies to perianth, segment and tepal. Without the rule, tepal plus outer keeps the whorl. The previous review's acceptance of 'outer tepal' (C374) came before that context word existed.
Plural of R3121.
Same as R3121. 'Outer' plus 'tepals' gives tepal (PO_0009033) plus outer (FLOPO_0991379).

target: plant cell part of leaf base (PO_0009002; container leaf base PO_0020040)
why: Marginal basal cells are not alar cells (alar cells are at the basal angles). Follows 'leaf sheath cell' (R3694): a plant cell plus the moss leaf base it belongs to. 'Marginal' is a position and is read separately (pattern 04).

target: plant cell part of leaf base (PO_0009002; container leaf base PO_0020040)
why: Plural of 'marginal basal cell'. Same treatment, not alar cell.

A bare 'sinker' is ambiguous: in mistletoes (Loranthaceae, Viscaceae) it is the feeding organ that grows into the host (a haustorium), not a root, and elsewhere it is a descending root. No single class fits.
Plural of the ambiguous bare 'sinker' (mistletoe feeding organ or root). Same as R3260.

A panicled cyme is a branched (panicle-like) group of cymes, close to a thyrse. As a whole it is not a PO cyme inflorescence. PO splits thyrse into determinate and indeterminate classes, and earlier reviews used the value thyrse-like (FLOPO:0991199) for that reason. No bearer rule fits safely.
Same as R3270.

PO has no sporangiophore class. PO sporophyll is 'a leaf-like organ bearing sporangia', but the stalked, shield-shaped (peltate) sporangiophores of Equisetum are not clearly leaf-like, and in fungi the word means something else. Leave unmapped or ask for a new class.
Plural of sporangiophore. Same as R3272.

'Costal vein' is ambiguous. In ferns it is a vein along the costa (the midrib of a pinna, sometimes forming small closed areas), and elsewhere it is a vein near the midrib or margin. It is not reliably a secondary vein, and no single PO class fits.
Plural of costal vein. Same as R3279.

A pseudolocule is a cavity made by a secondary false septum (Vaccinium), not a true locule of the carpel. Mapping it to locule would turn '10-pseudoloculed' into 10 locules, which is false (5 true locules). It needs its own class or no rule.
Same as R3327: a false locule is not a locule, and mapping it would give wrong locule counts.
This is an adjective (having false locules), not a part name. Like R3327, it must not count as locules, so it should also not be added to flora_counted_parts.tsv.

In Nymphaeaceae the disk is not the stigma. In Nuphar the stigmatic disk is the flattened top of the ovary, with the stigmatic rays lying on it. In Nymphaea the stigmas sit in a cup, and the carpel tips (stigmatic appendages) stand around it. Its qualities in the data ('entire to crenate', 'occasion

PO gemma (PO_0025614) is defined as a small ball of cells borne on a thallus. The data (Isopterygium, Pseudotaxiphyllum) describe uniseriate filamentous axillary propagula on leafy mosses, which do not fit that definition. The phrase also covers bulbils and brood bodies. No single existing class fit

Anther tails are usually basal extensions of the thecae (Asteraceae caudate anthers, Ericaceae), not connective appendages. There is no existing thecal-appendage class, so no rule should map this word.

Pseudostaminode is mainly an Amaranthaceae term. 'Interstaminal appendage' is broader: it also covers interstaminal staminodes (Sapotaceae), filament-tube teeth and corona lobes. There is also a conflict: R2353 already maps 'pseudo-staminode' to staminode (PO_0009077). Do not add a third route.

'Corolla scale' covers Cuscuta infrastaminal scales, Boraginaceae fornices (already faucal appendage, FLOPO_0986115), Caryophyllaceae and Sapindaceae petal scales, and coronal scales. No single class fits.

The data already mix meanings. Monanthotaxis (Annonaceae) has segments of moniliform monocarps ('segments globose'), and Ormocarpum has loment joints. 'Fruit segment' is also used for mericarps and citrus segments.

PO keeps teeth and lobes apart as separate classes (leaf lamina tooth PO_0025518 next to the lobe classes). Mapping teeth to involucre lobe would break that split, and we have no tooth class for the involucre. It needs an involucre-tooth class or a 'tooth part of involucre' pattern.
Adjective form of R3520; drop for the same reason.

'Syngenesious' says the anthers are fused into a tube. That is a quality of the anthers (connate), not the name of a part. Mapping it to anther tube loses the fusion statement. Handle it as anther plus a connate quality, by a pattern.

Palms have an adaxial and an abaxial hastula, and they often differ: one present and the other absent, or of different shape. Mapping both to the same 'hastula' makes 'adaxial hastula present, abaxial absent' contradict itself. This needs subclasses or a position qualifier, not this rule.
Same as R3573. Losing the position creates false contradictions.

Corolla appendages include coronas, ligules and scales outside the throat, so 'faucal' is too narrow. No existing general class for corolla appendages was found (only connective appendage and anther theca appendage). A new class is needed, not this rule.

Bare 'propagule' also means a fruit or seed diaspore (PO has 'propagule' as a synonym of fruit, PO_0009001) and the viviparous seedling of mangroves. It is ambiguous. The specific forms 'vegetative propagule' and 'brood body' are enough.
'Green cells' is vague. It is not the specific chlorophyllose cell type of Sphagnum or Leucobryum.

'Dorsal wing' is used for seed, fruit, calyx and keel wings, and only sometimes for the Fissidens dorsal lamina. Even with a leaf context it is doubtful, so reject it. The rule 'dorsal lamina' covers the moss sense.

The marginal cell of a lamella is a cell, not the lamella, so the target is wrong. Mapping it to a plain cell of the lamella would lose 'marginal', and the shape of the marginal cell (retuse, papillose, and so on) is the key Polytrichaceae character. Statements would be given to all lamella cells. T

The word names the wall of the leaf-blade cells, not the cell. PO has no cell-wall class; the cell wall is a GO class (GO:0005618). The previous review rejected every '... cell wall' bearer for this reason: 'basal cell wall', 'marginal cell wall', 'juxtacostal cell wall', 'inner walls'. Mapping to n

Non-vascular leaf (PO_0025075) is right only for bryophytes such as Sphagnum. 'Branch leaf' also turns up for conifers, lycophytes and other vascular plants. Leaf (PO_0025034) is the common parent of the vascular and non-vascular leaf, so it is correct in both groups and stays a part of the branch.

Use the same cell class as the sibling rules 'leaf cell' (R3661) and 'medial laminal cells' (R3735): plant cell PO_0009002, not native plant cell PO_0025606. 'Distal' cells in moss leaves are the cells of the upper blade, which is wider than the leaf apex. So leaf apex (PO_0020137, used for 'apical

These are cells of the photosynthetic filaments that grow on the upper surface of the costa (Aloina, Pterygoneurum). The statements describe the filaments (cell shape, papillae, cells per filament), not ordinary costa cells. Mapping to 'plant cell part of costa' would mix the two. The previous revie

target: plant cell (PO_0009002) part of seed coat (PO_0009088)
why: In the one source flora the statements (domed, smooth, papillate, elongate) are about the surface cells.
